opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Andrew Mann (E014) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Write is at or below the maximum, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Andrew Mann (E014): contractor with basic security training. Contractors max at read unless they have advanced training. Requested write is above the maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The HR and Security agents disagree on Andrew Mann's (E014) employment type: HR lists full_time (recommending write), while Security lists contractor with basic security training (recommending read). Under the contractor classification with only basic training, the maximum allowed access is read, and write would exceed that maximum. Given the conflicting employment-status evidence, granting read is the safe level that complies with the policy under either classification (full-time employees may have read, and contractors with basic training max out at read). I grant read.
